I farm 12 mu here in Quzhou County on alluvial soil that's somewhat alkaline but grows good grain if you feed it right. I keep 8 mu in the wheat-maize double crop because that's my foundation — it puts food on the table and pays for the inputs. The other 4 mu I split into 2 mu of chili and 2 mu of cotton, because cash crops are what cover my medical bills and house repairs. My wife and I are only two people now, so I hire two temporary workers during wheat harvest and maize sowing — that ten-day window is impossible alone, and every day of delay on summer maize costs me 5 to 7 kg per mu.

For winter wheat, I sowed an improved variety last October at 12.5 kg of seed per mu. Last year I put down 16 kg N per mu and got 550 kg per mu. Old Wang from the east end of the village used 18 kg N and hit 580 kg, and his soil is no better than mine. So this year I'm matching him — 18 kg N per mu total, split between basal compound fertilizer and urea topdressing at jointing. I also apply 7 kg P₂O₅ per mu and 6 kg K₂O per mu. I buy compound fertilizer 15-15-15 at 3,200 yuan per ton and urea at 2,400 yuan per ton. For the 8 mu of wheat, that's roughly 25 kg of compound per mu as basal, plus about 22 kg of urea per mu topdressed. I irrigate three times: spring green-up water, jointing stage, and grain filling. Two pesticide sprays — one for powdery mildew at jointing and one for aphids at heading. I'm targeting 580 kg per mu.

Summer maize is Zhengdan 958 hybrid at 2.5 kg seed per mu, planted immediately after wheat harvest in early June. I use no-tillage — just drill straight into the wheat stubble. There's no time to plough; the heat builds fast and the seedling stage is short. I apply 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer 28-6-6 at sowing, then topdress with 15 kg urea per mu at the large flare stage. That works out to 15 kg N per mu, 5 kg P₂O₅ per mu, and 5 kg K₂O per mu. Two irrigations: one at jointing and one at filling. Two pesticide applications for corn borer and aphids. Expected yield is 600 kg per mu.

For chili, I buy hybrid seedlings from the dealer in town at about 300 yuan per mu. I rotary till the 2 mu plot and transplant in late April. Chili is hungry for potassium — without it the peppers stay small and thin-walled. I apply 14 kg N per mu, 7 kg P₂O₅ per mu, and 12 kg K₂O per mu using compound fertilizer plus potassium sulfate. Five irrigations through the season, roughly every 12 to 15 days in July and August. Four pesticide sprays because aphids and viral disease come fast when it's hot and humid. I expect 2,500 kg per mu of fresh chili, which I sun-dry on plastic sheets and sell.

Cotton gets 2 mu. I plough deep in early spring — cotton roots need loose soil down to 25 cm or the bolls don't set well. I sow Bt hybrid cotton in mid-April. I learned the hard way about ten years ago that too much nitrogen makes cotton shoot up to my waist without bolls. So I hold it to 13 kg N per mu, 6 kg P₂O₅ per mu, and 8 kg K₂O per mu. Three irrigations: at flowering, at boll setting, and once more in late August if the weather turns dry. Even with Bt cotton, I spray three times for red spider mite and leaf spot. Expected seed cotton yield is 350 kg per mu.

My total fertilizer bill for the 12 mu this year is about 6,800 yuan. I thought about cutting back on chili potassium to save 400 yuan, but if I lose even 200 kg per mu of fresh chili on 2 mu, that's 400 kg gone — worth over 2,000 yuan after drying and selling. I'd rather spend the money. A bad harvest is a disaster I cannot afford; wasting a bit of fertilizer is just a cost I can absorb.
